test_title: PYST 6: SSC CGL 2022 - English (Held On: 06 Dec 2022 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
**The question below consists of a set of labeled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P. There once was a little boy who had a very bad temper.

Q. The boy gradually began to control his temper over the next few weeks, and the number of nails he was hammering into the fence slowly decreased.

R. His father decided to hand him a bag of nails and said that every time the boy lost his temper, he had to hammer a nail into the fence.

S. On the first day, the boy hammered 37 nails into that fence.
solution:
The correct answer is **"PRSQ"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate answer to the given question is** "PRSQ"**
 
• By reading all the sentences it is clear that** sentence P** is the introductory statement.
 
• The **sentence R** should come second because it is indicating the solution to the problem of the boy.
 
• By carefully reading the remaining sentences it is clear that **sentence S **will come next because it is in continuation with** **sentence R.
 
• **Sentence Q **will come last because it is indicating the outcome of the solution mentioned in sentence R.
 
• Therefore, the correct order is **'PRSQ.'**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**​

 
• The correct logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph is as follows:
 
• *There once was a little boy who had a very bad temper. His father decided to hand him a bag of nails and said that every time the boy lost his temper, he had to hammer a nail into the fence. On the first day, the boy hammered 37 nails into that fence. The boy gradually began to control his temper over the next few weeks, and the number of nails he was hammering into the fence slowly decreased.*
